title: Current limit: clamp window over PVT, non-engagement at 50mA, and a held Vout=0 short
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Current limit" row (constant-current (brickwall) clamp, window TBD over PVT; never engages for I_load <= 50 mA; survives continuous Vout = 0 short at Vin_max) against the sense-FET current comparator and gate clamp issue #22 added to design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch (M_SENSE / M_CLN1 / M_CLN2 / M_CLP / M_CLIM -- see design/README.md's "Current limit (#22)"). The row is ratified by issue #1 / DR-006 and it deliberately carries NO numeric clamp window: the window is "TBD over PVT". This experiment therefore splits the row rather than blurring it -- the clauses that carry a number are bounded below ("never engages for I_load <= 50 mA" becomes ilim_short_ma/ilim_knee_ma > 50 mA plus vout_50ma_v inside the ratified Output row's 1.764-1.836 V window), and the clause that does not ("window TBD over PVT", "survives") is measured and reported WITHOUT a bound, because establishing that window over PVT is exactly what the row asks for at this stage; inventing a ceiling would be the invented settled number CLAUDE.md forbids. "At Vin_max" is covered by the corner runner's own supply axis (the 3.63 V column), not by a hard-coded VIN. Legs 1 and 3 are both `tran ... uic` with EN rising at t=100us, so each reaches regulation through a real soft-start ramp from a cold start rather than from an ngspice operating-point solve of the fully-enabled loop: the initial-condition contract's first accepted shape (uic + an EN edge -- sim/README.md, issue #171). Issue #76 gave leg 3 its EN edge after PR #75 shipped the same fix in sim/startup and sim/enable-shutdown (the ff/sf 125C nuisance-trip mechanism of issue #69); issue #177 then replaced leg 1's bare unseeded `op` with the same transient AND added the `uic` keyword to both legs, because the EN edge alone does not remove the hazard: ngspice solves a transient operating point before a non-uic tran, and for a source carrying both a dc value and a transient function that solve uses the DC value ('vsup', fully enabled -- ngspice prints "Note: ven: dc value used for op instead of transient time=0 value" on stderr every run), which #177 measured tripping `Warning: Dynamic gmin stepping failed` on BOTH transient legs. `uic` skips that solve; measurements are unchanged by it. Leg 2's `dc` sweep is the one analysis that still solves with EN at its dc value, and that is not the forbidden shape: the forcing branch (RFORCE = 1 mOhm) pins VOUT at every swept point, so there is no free regulating branch for the solver to pick, each point after the first continues from the previous point's converged solution, and #177 measured it emitting no solver-diagnostic marker (its gmin stepping completes rather than failing). The short is applied as an event at t=1.0ms -- after sim/startup's measured 0.26-0.45ms soft-start ramp completes -- and HELD to t=3.0ms: 2 ms of continuous Vout = 0, a defined duration rather than a single sampled instant, since "survives" is a claim about holding the fault. Known-caveat, stated rather than hidden (design/README.md, "Known accuracy caveat"): M_SENSE is a 0.42um replica of a 2500um pass device whose drain does not sit at VOUT, so the 1:5952 ratio is neither Vds-matched nor trimmed and carries substantial random Vth mismatch -- this corner-matrix experiment measures the systematic PVT window only; the mismatch axis would need a Monte Carlo experiment (sim/bin/mc-run.py), which is not in this issue's scope.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

analyses: * --- leg 1: 50 mA operating point (RFORCE open) -- the clamp must be OFF ---
* Initial-condition contract (sim/README.md, issue #171; converted by issue #177):
* this leg used to be a bare unseeded `op`, which VEN's dc value ('vsup') solved
* with the loop already fully enabled -- exactly the from-nowhere Newton start the
* contract forbids. It is now a `tran ... uic` whose EN edge at t=100-101us brings
* the block up through its own soft-start ramp: the contract's first accepted
* shape (uic + an EN edge), the same one sim/mc-output-accuracy uses post-#164.
* The `uic` keyword is load-bearing and NOT redundant with VEN's pwl starting at
* 0 V: ngspice performs a transient operating-point solve before a non-uic tran,
* and for a source that carries BOTH a dc value and a transient function that
* solve uses the DC VALUE -- ngspice says so itself, on stderr, every run:
*   Note: ven: dc value used for op instead of transient time=0 value.
* so a non-uic tran here would still solve the fully-enabled, loop-closed state
* from ngspice's own guess (issue #177 measured that solve tripping
* `Warning: Dynamic gmin stepping failed` at tt/27C/3.30V, i.e. corner-run.py's
* solver-diagnostic FAIL gate) even though the transient WAVEFORM does start from
* the pwl's t=0 value. `uic` skips that solve outright.
* 5 us max timestep (leg 3 keeps 500 ns because it has to resolve the 1 us
* short edge; this leg has no fast event, so it uses the same 5 us ceiling
* sim/enable-shutdown's tran does -- the EN PWL's 100/101 us corners are
* breakpoints and are honoured regardless).
tran 5u 1.0m uic
meas tran vout_50ma avg v(vout) from=0.9m to=1.0m
meas tran vout_50ma_lo min v(vout) from=0.9m to=1.0m
meas tran vout_50ma_hi max v(vout) from=0.9m to=1.0m
meas tran vin_50ma avg v(vin) from=0.9m to=1.0m
meas tran cl_cmp_50ma avg v(xldo.cl_cmp) from=0.9m to=1.0m
* --- leg 2: DC limit characteristic, VOUT forced from 0 V up to 1.75 V ---
alter rload = 1e12
alter rforce = 1m
dc vforce 0 1.75 0.125
meas dc ilim_short find i(vforce) at=0
meas dc ilim_knee find i(vforce) at=1.75
* --- leg 3: cold EN ramp (t=100-101us), Vout=0 short applied at t=1.0ms (after soft-start settles) and HELD to t=3.0ms ---
* Also `uic`, and for exactly the reason leg 1 is (issue #177). Issue #174's audit
* recorded leg 3 as NOT exposed on the theory that a non-uic tran seeds itself from
* VEN's pwl value at t=0 (0 V, disabled). That theory is wrong about the op solve:
* #177 measured this leg, run non-uic and on its own, tripping the same
* `Warning: Dynamic gmin stepping failed` leg 1 did -- from the dc-valued transient
* operating point, before the first timestep. `uic` removes it, with bit-identical
* measurements (ish_avg -1.53348e-01 A both ways at tt/27C/3.30V).
alter rload = 36
tran 500n 3.0m uic
meas tran ipre avg i(vvin) from=0.9m to=1.0m
meas tran ish_avg avg i(vvin) from=2.0m to=3.0m
meas tran ish_max max i(vvin) from=1.1m to=3.0m
meas tran ish_min min i(vvin) from=1.1m to=3.0m
meas tran vsh_max max v(vout) from=1.1m to=3.0m

measurements.name: vout_50ma_v
measurements.note: VOUT at a 36 Ohm (~50 mA) load with the forcing branch absent, averaged over t = 0.9-1.0 ms of leg 1's `tran ... uic` -- i.e. after the block has powered up through its own soft-start ramp from a cold start (issue #177; the same 0.9-1.0 ms pre-fault window leg 3's isup_pre_short_ma already uses). Before #177 this read a bare unseeded `op`, which the initial-condition contract (sim/README.md, issue #171) forbids. This is the operative form of the ratified "Current limit" row's "never engages for I_load <= 50 mA" clause: if the clamp engaged anywhere at or below the ratified Load row's 50 mA ceiling, the loop would stop regulating. Bound cited: spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Output" row (1.8 V +-2%, i.e. 1.764-1.836 V) -- ratified by issue #1 / DR-006, cited verbatim, not an invented limit.

measurements.name: vout_50ma_span_v
measurements.note: Peak-to-peak VOUT over the same t = 0.9-1.0 ms window (unbounded, diagnostic). The settledness witness leg 1 needs now that its 50 mA point is read off a transient rather than an `op`: a small span is what says the averaged value above is a settled operating point and not a snapshot of a ramp still in motion (issue #177's three quick corners measured 4e-6 to 4.7e-5 V, i.e. settled to within tens of microvolts). Modelled on sim/ic-screen-125c-b's vout_tail_span, added by issue #177 with the leg-1 conversion. Reported, not bounded -- the ratified row sets no settling criterion, and inventing one here would be the invented number CLAUDE.md forbids; the bounded claim is vout_50ma_v itself.

measurements.name: cl_margin_50ma_v
measurements.note: VIN - V(CL_CMP) at the same 50 mA point (both averaged over t = 0.9-1.0 ms of leg 1's `tran ... uic`), read hierarchically from the DUT's current-limit comparison node. Per design/README.md's node glossary CL_CMP ~= VIN means the comparator is inactive and M_CLIM is off; CL_CMP falls when the limit engages. Reported, not bounded: turning "how far from engaging" into a pass/fail needs a threshold the ratified row does not state (its window is "TBD over PVT"), so this experiment measures the margin instead of grading it.

measurements.name: ilim_short_ma
measurements.note: LDO output current with VOUT forced to 0 V (dead short), from the DC characteristic. Lower bound 50 mA is the ratified row's own "never engages for I_load <= 50 mA" clause read as a limit-level requirement -- the clamp cannot sit at or below the load the block is specified to deliver. NO upper bound: the row says the clamp window is "TBD over PVT", so this experiment's job for that clause is to establish the window, not to grade it against a number nobody has ratified. Issue #1 / DR-006 ratified the row with that window deliberately left as "TBD over PVT", so only a future decision record can set it; if one does, this measurement acquires a max and nothing else here changes.

measurements.name: ilim_knee_ma
measurements.note: LDO output current with VOUT forced to 1.75 V -- the knee just below the regulation point, i.e. the lowest limit level the block can reach while the output is still near its target. Same ratified-row-derived 50 mA lower bound and same deliberately-absent upper bound as ilim_short_ma. Together the two values ARE the PVT window the row asks to be established.

measurements.name: ilim_droop_pct
measurements.note: Shape indicator for the row's "constant-current (brickwall)" word, as the fall in limit current from the 1.75 V knee down to the dead short, in percent of the knee value. A foldback limiter's short-circuit current is well BELOW its knee current (large positive droop); a constant-current clamp's is not (~0 or negative). Reported, not bounded: the row names the shape but sets no numeric flatness criterion, and a knife-edge bound at zero would grade solver noise rather than topology.

measurements.name: ishort_sustained_ma
measurements.note: Mean supply current over the last 1 ms of the held Vout = 0 short (t = 2.0-3.0 ms), i.e. the current the pass device actually sustains into a continuous short. Read from i(vvin) rather than i(vforce) on purpose: i(vforce) also carries C_OUT's ~2 A microsecond discharge spike into the short, which is the capacitor's stored energy and not the pass device's current. Reported, not bounded, for the same reason as ilim_short_ma: the ratified row's window is TBD. This is the number the Thermal row's "short-circuit ceiling set by the current limit" will need once this row's PVT window is established.

measurements.name: ishort_ripple_pct
measurements.note: Peak-to-peak variation of the supply current across the whole held-short window (t = 1.1-3.0 ms), in percent of its mean. This is the one part of "survives a continuous short" that can be bounded without inventing a number: the row calls the clamp "constant-current", and a limit loop swinging by more than its own mean is not delivering a constant current -- it is limit-cycling. 100% is therefore the weakest non-arbitrary reading of the row's own word, chosen deliberately over a tighter invented figure; a healthy clamp measures far below it.

measurements.name: vout_short_mv
measurements.note: Highest VOUT reached during the held short (t = 1.1-3.0 ms). Reported as a sanity witness that the fault really was a Vout = 0 short for its whole 2 ms duration (the forcing branch is 1 mOhm, so this is essentially I_short x 1 mOhm), not as a spec bound.

measurements.name: isup_pre_short_ma
measurements.note: Mean VIN supply current over the 100 us immediately before the short is applied. Reported to document the pre-fault condition the short is applied FROM: the output node is held at the nominal 1.8 V by the forcing branch (still at 1 mOhm from the DC leg) while the 36 Ohm load draws ~50 mA, so the loop is live and delivering into a node at its own regulation target -- an active, at-target block, NOT an idle or cold-start one. Because the forcing source and the LDO share that 50 mA load, this value is the LDO's own contribution only and is expected to be well below 50 mA (the forcing source supplies the remainder); it is reported rather than bounded for exactly that reason. What matters for the "survives" clause is that the fault is applied to a live loop at its nominal output, which this measurement witnesses and vout_short_mv confirms the fault itself.
